subsystems.name: Voxel medium
subsystems.role: the physical thing in mid-air that scatters or emits light so a viewer sees a point of image.
parts: ionised air (plasma) from a focused pulsed laser
near-eye retinal projection (virtual image in the eye instead of in the room)

subsystems.name: Emitter and scanner
subsystems.role: places each voxel at the right coordinate thousands of times per second.
parts: scanning mirrors or spatial light modulators

subsystems.name: Spatial sensing
subsystems.role: knows where the user's head, hands and the room's surfaces are.

subsystems.name: Spatial audio
subsystems.role: gives interface elements a position you can hear.

subsystems.name: Compute and render stack
subsystems.role: turns an application's 3D scene into a timed stream of voxel coordinates.

subsystems.name: Holographic OS layer
subsystems.role: the actual operating system: window manager for volumes, input model, permissions, app framework.

subsystems.name: Safety envelope
subsystems.role: keeps lasers and ultrasound from injuring eyes, skin or lungs, and manages exhaust gases.

buildSteps.title: Choose the voxel mechanism
buildSteps.detail: Decide how light will exist in empty space. Options in the lab are laser-induced plasma, a laser-trapped particle, an ultrasonically levitated bead, or projection straight into the viewer's eye. Each choice fixes the rest of the design.

buildSteps.title: Build the emitter array
buildSteps.detail: Assemble and align lasers with scanning optics, or an ultrasonic phased array with a trap beam, so voxels can be addressed in three dimensions across the intended volume.

buildSteps.title: Solve safety and containment
buildSteps.detail: Focused laser pulses must be eye-safe and enclosed in a managed field of view; plasma in air makes ozone and nitrogen oxides that need ventilation; high-intensity ultrasound must stay within heating limits. This step, not the optics, is what decides whether the device can sit in a home.

buildSteps.title: Make the render pipeline
buildSteps.detail: Write a volumetric renderer and a scheduler that fires every voxel in the right order. Like a CRT, the image relies on persistence: the whole volume must be redrawn faster than the eye can follow, so brightness and complexity trade off directly against refresh rate.

buildSteps.title: Add tracking and audio
buildSteps.detail: Depth cameras and inertial sensors track head and hands so the interface is anchored to real space; a head-tracked binaural renderer gives each element a sound position.

buildSteps.title: Write the OS layer
buildSteps.detail: Build a compositor that manages 3D regions the way a desktop manages windows, plus a spatial input model, an app framework, permissions for cameras and microphones, and a way for apps to declare how much of the volume they occupy.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and stress-test
buildSteps.detail: Optical and geometric calibration keeps voxels where the renderer thinks they are as the hardware warms and ages; latency, occlusion and multi-user viewing are measured and iterated.

buildSteps.title: Productise
buildSteps.detail: Shrink power, cooling and optics into something affordable and quiet, and decide the honest target: a controlled desktop volume, a near-eye display that merely looks free-space, or a whole room.

prerequisites.tech: Free-space voxel generation bright enough to see in daylight
prerequisites.why: plasma and trapped-particle displays demonstrated so far are dim, tiny and monochrome-ish; nothing yet scales to a room-sized, daylight-readable volume.

prerequisites.tech: Real-time volumetric rendering and low-latency tracking
prerequisites.why: modern headsets already render stereo 3D with head tracking at low latency, and that pipeline is reusable.
headset operating systems with 3D window managers and hand tracking exist, but only behind a display, not in open air.

prerequisites.tech: Eye-safe laser and ultrasound exposure frameworks
prerequisites.why: laser and ultrasound safety standards exist and would constrain brightness, range and refresh rate for any free-space display.
a volume of light has no solid surfaces to block what is behind it, so depth cues collapse for anyone but a single tracked viewer.

pathway.unlocks: proven 3D window management, hand tracking and app ecosystems — the software half of a holographic OS.

pathway.milestone: near-eye light-field and holographic displays that remove bulky optics
pathway.unlocks: thin, comfortable devices with convincing depth, still worn rather than floating in the room.

pathway.milestone: lab-scale free-space volumetric displays of useful brightness and size
pathway.unlocks: single-user interfaces that genuinely exist in mid-air inside a desk-sized safe volume.

pathway.milestone: room-scale, multi-user, daylight-visible volumetric display with safe power and ventilation
pathway.unlocks: a true holographic operating system, replacing screens rather than supplementing them.
